claims.text: Llívia is a town in Catalonia, Spain; it is a Spanish exclave surrounded by the French département of Pyrénées-Orientales.
Llívia has a population of 1,562 (register office, 2025).
Llívia is separated from the rest of Spain by a corridor about 1.6 km wide, including the French communes of Ur and Bourg-Madame.
The corridor is traversed by a road owned by both France and Spain; since the Schengen Area in 1995 there have been no formal borders.
The 1659 Treaty of the Pyrenees ceded only villages to France; Llívia was a town, so it remained a Spanish enclave.
